key_insight: AI agents discovered quantum programs with formally verified correctness and cost, achieving substantial improvements over prior baselines.
engineering_relevance: Formal verification enables quantum algorithm development beyond classically testable regimes, potentially reducing resource requirements for scientific applications.
method: Build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover.
Have language-model agents synthesize programs against formal specifications and verify correctness and cost.
Coordinate agent teams through shared wikis and organized conferences.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over prior baselines of up to 1.4× for parallel search, 290× for quantum arithmetic, and 11×, 8× and 2.5× for simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug metabolism, respectively.
watch_item: Verified correctness and cost do not establish practical hardware speedups; deployment depends on physical implementation and resource overheads.
paper_title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
